key_finding: POET in FY2025 is the textbook pre-commercial-revenue photonics platform balance sheet story. Operating losses are real ($63M net loss, $18M R&D) and revenue is essentially zero (Q3 $298K and Q4 $341K of NRE-and-product), but the asset base grew from $69.7M (Dec 2024) to $328.6M (Dec 2025) — a near 5x balance sheet expansion driven by a $250M institutional equity raise. Cash and short-term investments stand at $313.4M, providing roughly 5 years of runway at the FY25 burn rate. The dilution overhang is meaningful: 5.79M options and 37.36M warrants outstanding against 132.3M common shares = potential 28.35% dilution. A $135.6M derivative warrant liability sits on the balance sheet as one of the most consequential single line items.

annual_revenue_history_usd_thousands.note: Revenue is non-recurring engineering (NRE) and small product revenue. POET remains essentially pre-commercial.

us250m_institutional_equity_financing.buyer_names: Not publicly disclosed at snapshot date
us250m_institutional_equity_financing.transaction_significance: Funded the 5x balance sheet expansion and provides ~5 years of runway at FY25 burn rate

structural_observations: FY25 revenue of ~$1.2M does not cover even one quarter of the $18M R&D run rate — POET is a pure platform-bet equity story, not an operating company.
$313.4M cash + short-term investments provides multi-year runway. At FY25 burn rate of ~$45M cash operating loss (net loss $63M less $18M non-cash), runway is approximately 7 years.
Warrant liability of $135.6M is a non-cash mark-to-market item but represents real economic obligation; exercise would dilute shareholders by up to 28% from current share count.
Accumulated deficit of ~$297M provides historical context: POET has consumed roughly $297M of cumulative equity in pursuit of the platform thesis before reaching commercial revenue.

20-F filing basis means POET is a Canadian foreign private issuer in US SEC parlance. The dual NASDAQ + TSX listing is structural — TSX provides the home-country listing, NASDAQ provides US institutional access.
